senses.def: the act or process of making or producing something
examples: The documentary shows the making of the film.
She has a small business in jewelry making.

senses.def: the qualities needed to become a particular thing
examples: The young player has the makings of a future star.

note: "History in the making" = something important happening now. "A problem of your own making" = one you caused yourself.

senses.def: belonging to the sex that does not give birth, or connected with men
examples: Most of the company's senior managers are male.
A male lion can weigh over 400 pounds.

senses.def: a male person, animal or plant
examples: The suspect is a white male in his thirties.
In many bird species, the male is more colorful than the female.

note: "Male" as a noun for people sounds clinical (police, science reports). In everyday speech say "man".

senses.def: a large building or covered area with many stores and restaurants
examples: Teenagers like to hang out at the mall on weekends.
The new mall has over two hundred stores.

note: American English. British English often says "shopping centre".

senses.def: an adult male human
examples: A man in a gray suit was waiting outside the office.
He's a kind, honest man.

senses.def: humans in general (old-fashioned)
examples: Fire was one of man's most important discoveries.

senses.def: used to express surprise, anger or excitement (informal)
examples: Man, that was a long drive!

note: Plural: men. For humans in general, "people" or "humanity" is preferred today. "Best man" = sağdıç.

senses.def: to be in charge of a business, team or organization
examples: She manages a team of twelve engineers.
He used to manage a hotel in Las Vegas.

senses.def: to succeed in doing something difficult
examples: Somehow we managed to finish the project on time.
Did you manage to find a parking space?

senses.def: to be able to deal with problems or live without much money or help
examples: I don't know how they manage on such a small income.

note: "Manage to do" means you succeeded despite difficulty: I managed to fix it (= düzeltmeyi başardım).

senses.def: the activity of running and controlling a business or organization
examples: She has a degree in business management.
Good time management is key to success in college.

senses.def: the people who run a company or organization
examples: Management refused to meet with the union.
The hotel is under new management.

senses.def: a person in charge of running a business, store or department
examples: I'd like to speak to the manager, please.
She was promoted to sales manager last year.

senses.def: a person who manages an athlete, performer or sports team
examples: The band fired their manager after a dispute over money.

note: In US sports, the head of a baseball team is the "manager"; for most other sports it's the "head coach".

senses.def: the authority given to a government or leader by the people who voted for them
examples: The new president has a clear mandate for change.
The election gave the party a strong mandate.

senses.def: an official order or requirement to do something
examples: The state lifted its mask mandate in the spring.

senses.def: to officially order or require something
examples: The law mandates that all new buildings have solar panels.

note: Formal. In US English the verb "mandate" (= require by law) is very common in news.

senses.def: required by law or by a rule
examples: Wearing a seat belt is mandatory in all states.
Attendance at the safety meeting is mandatory for all staff.

note: Opposite: optional / voluntary. Americans use "mandatory" more than "compulsory".

senses.def: to show something clearly, or to appear or become noticeable
examples: The disease can manifest itself in many different ways.
Her anxiety manifested as constant headaches.

senses.def: easy to see or understand (formal)
examples: His disappointment was manifest to everyone in the room.

senses.def: a list of the cargo or passengers on a ship or plane
examples: The passenger's name did not appear on the flight manifest.

note: Formal. Often reflexive: "manifest itself". In pop culture, "manifest" also means to attract something by believing in it.

senses.def: to control or influence someone or something in a clever, often unfair way
examples: He manipulated his friends into lending him money.
The company was accused of manipulating the figures.

senses.def: to control or handle something with skill, especially with your hands or a computer
examples: The software lets you manipulate photos easily.

senses.def: controlling or influencing someone or something in a clever and unfair way
examples: The bank was fined for market manipulation.
Emotional manipulation is a common sign of an abusive relationship.

senses.def: the skillful handling or processing of something
examples: The course covers data manipulation in spreadsheets.

senses.def: the way that something is done or happens
examples: The issue was handled in a professional manner.
Complaints should be dealt with in a timely manner.

senses.def: the way someone behaves toward other people
examples: She has a calm, friendly manner with patients.

senses.def: polite behavior that is acceptable in a particular society
examples: It's bad manners to talk with your mouth full.
Her kids have excellent manners.

note: "Manners" (plural) = politeness. "All manner of" (formal) = many different kinds of.

senses.tr: elle yapılan, bedensel (iş); manuel, el ile çalışan
senses.def: done with the hands, or operated by hand rather than automatically
examples: He worked in manual jobs before going to college.
I learned to drive in a car with a manual transmission.

senses.def: a book that tells you how to do something or use a machine
examples: Check the user manual before you set up the printer.
The staff manual explains the company's policies.

note: Opposite: automatic. A car with a manual transmission is called a "stick shift" in informal American English.

senses.def: to make goods in large quantities, using machines
examples: The company manufactures parts for electric cars.
Most of these toys are manufactured in Asia.

senses.def: to invent something such as a story or excuse in order to trick people
examples: The evidence against him was manufactured by police.

senses.def: the process of producing goods in large quantities
examples: The chemicals are used in the manufacture of plastics.

senses.def: the business or industry of producing goods in large quantities
examples: Many manufacturing jobs have moved overseas.
The region's economy was built on manufacturing.

senses.def: a writer's copy of a book or article before it is published
examples: She sent her manuscript to over twenty publishers.
Please submit your manuscript by the end of June.

senses.def: a very old book or document written by hand
examples: The library holds rare medieval manuscripts.

senses.def: a large number of (used with plural nouns)
examples: Many people work from home now.
There aren't many good restaurants in this area.

senses.def: a large number of people or things
examples: Many of the students failed the test.
I've seen a lot of his films, but not many recently.

note: Use "many" with countable nouns (many books) and "much" with uncountable nouns (much time). In positive sentences, "a lot of" is more natural.

senses.def: a drawing or plan of an area showing roads, towns, rivers, etc.
examples: Check the map to see how far it is to the next town.
I use the map on my phone to get around the city.

senses.def: to make a map of an area, or find out and record the details of something
examples: Scientists have mapped the entire human genome.
The satellite will map the ocean floor.

note: "Put somewhere on the map" = make it famous. "Map out" = plan in detail.

senses.def: a running race of about 42 kilometers (26.2 miles)
examples: She ran her first marathon in under four hours.
Thousands of runners took part in the Boston Marathon.

senses.def: an activity that lasts a long time and needs a lot of effort
examples: The negotiations turned into a twelve-hour marathon.
We had a movie marathon all weekend.

note: "It's a marathon, not a sprint" = success takes patience and steady effort.

senses.def: an organized walk by many people to protest or support something
examples: Thousands joined the march for climate action.
The civil rights march ended at the Capitol.

senses.tr: uygun adım yürümek, tören yürüyüşü yapmak
senses.def: to walk with regular steps like a soldier
examples: The soldiers marched through the city center.

senses.def: to walk somewhere as a protest, or to walk quickly and angrily
examples: Students marched on City Hall to demand lower fees.
She marched into the office and demanded an apology.

senses.def: the third month of the year, between February and April
examples: My birthday is in March.
The new store opens on March 15.

note: Always capitalized. Use "in" for the month and "on" for a date: in March, on March 3.

senses.def: the empty space at the side of a written or printed page
examples: The teacher wrote comments in the margin of my essay.
Set the margins to one inch on all sides.

senses.def: the amount by which one thing is more or less than another, for example in a vote
examples: She won the election by a narrow margin.
The bill passed by a wide margin.

senses.def: the difference between the cost of something and the price it is sold for
examples: Grocery stores operate on very thin margins.

note: "On the margins of society" = excluded from the mainstream.

senses.def: small and not important
examples: The new policy made only a marginal difference.
There was a marginal increase in sales last month.

senses.def: not part of the main group or activity, and having little influence
examples: The party remained a marginal force in national politics.

note: Trap: Turkish "marjinal" often means "eccentric, unconventional". In English, "marginal" usually means small or unimportant.

senses.def: connected with the sea and the animals and plants that live there
examples: She studied marine biology in Florida.
Plastic pollution is a serious threat to marine life.

senses.def: a soldier trained to fight on land and at sea, especially in the US Marine Corps
examples: Her brother served as a Marine in Afghanistan.

note: Trap: Turkish "marina" is a boat harbor; "marine" is an adjective (deniz-) or a soldier.

senses.def: a small dirty area or damaged spot on a surface, or a written symbol
examples: The wine left a red mark on the tablecloth.
Put a check mark next to each correct answer.

senses.def: a particular level or point, or (British) a score given for work
examples: Unemployment has passed the 10 percent mark.

senses.def: to write or draw a sign on something to show something
examples: Mark the dates of your exams on the calendar.

senses.def: to celebrate or show that something is important, or to be a sign of a change
examples: The festival marks the beginning of spring.
The ceremony marked the 50th anniversary of the event.

note: "Make your mark" = become successful or noticed. Americans "grade" papers; British teachers "mark" them.

senses.def: an object or sign that shows the position of something or that something exists
examples: A stone marker shows where the battle took place.
High blood sugar can be a marker of diabetes.

senses.def: a pen with a thick felt tip
examples: She wrote the names on the whiteboard with a red marker.

senses.def: a place, often outdoors, where people buy and sell goods
examples: We buy fresh vegetables at the farmers' market every Saturday.
The old market is full of spice stalls.

senses.def: the trade in a particular type of goods, or the people who want to buy them
examples: The housing market has slowed down this year.
There's a growing market for plant-based food.

senses.def: to advertise and sell a product in a particular way
examples: The drink is marketed to young athletes.

note: Trap: Turkish "market" means a grocery store; in American English that's a "grocery store" or "supermarket". "On the market" = for sale.

senses.def: the activity of presenting, advertising and selling a product in the best way
examples: She works in marketing for a big sportswear brand.
The company spent millions on marketing for the new phone.

senses.def: the world of business and competition between companies
examples: Small firms struggle to compete in the global marketplace.
The product was a big hit in the marketplace.

senses.def: an open area where a market is held, or a website where people buy and sell
examples: I sold my old bike on an online marketplace.

senses.def: the legal relationship between two people who are married
examples: They have a happy marriage after thirty years together.
Same-sex marriage became legal nationwide in 2015.

senses.def: the ceremony in which two people get married
examples: Their marriage took place in a small church.

note: "Marriage" is the relationship; "wedding" is the ceremony/party. "Related by marriage" = in-laws.

senses.def: having a husband or wife
examples: Are you married or single?
They've been married for twelve years.

note: Use "married to", not "married with": She is married to a doctor. "Get married" is more common than "marry".

senses.def: to become someone's husband or wife
examples: He asked her to marry him on the beach.
They plan to marry next spring.

senses.def: to perform the ceremony in which two people get married
examples: The couple were married by a judge at City Hall.

note: No preposition: "She married him", not "married with him".

senses.def: connected with war, fighting or the army
examples: He has practiced martial arts like karate since he was six.
The government declared martial law after the coup.

note: Formal; mainly used in fixed phrases: martial arts (dövüş sanatları), martial law (sıkıyönetim).

senses.def: something worn over the face to hide it, protect it, or as part of a costume
examples: Doctors wear masks during surgery.
The robbers were wearing ski masks.

senses.def: a way of behaving that hides your real feelings
examples: Behind her mask of confidence, she was terrified.

senses.def: to hide a feeling, smell or fact so that it can't be noticed
examples: He tried to mask his disappointment with a smile.

senses.def: a large amount of a substance without a clear shape, or a large number of things together
examples: A mass of dark clouds moved across the sky.
There was a mass of people outside the stadium.

senses.def: ordinary people in general
examples: The smartphone brought the internet to the masses.

senses.def: affecting or involving a large number of people or things
examples: The factory closure led to mass unemployment in the town.
Police are investigating a mass shooting.

senses.def: the main religious ceremony in the Catholic Church
examples: They go to Mass every Sunday.

note: In physics, "mass" means the amount of matter in an object (kütle), not weight.

senses.def: the cruel killing of a large number of people, especially those who cannot defend themselves
examples: Hundreds of villagers died in the massacre.
The museum is dedicated to the victims of the massacre.

senses.def: to kill a large number of people in a cruel way
examples: Soldiers massacred civilians as they tried to flee.

note: Informally, a "massacre" in sports means a very heavy defeat.

senses.def: very large, heavy and solid
examples: A massive oak tree stood in the middle of the field.
The castle has massive stone walls.

senses.def: extremely large or serious in amount or degree
examples: He suffered a massive heart attack.
The movie was a massive success.

note: Trap: Turkish "masif" (solid wood) is narrower. English "massive" mostly means huge.

senses.def: to learn or understand something completely
examples: It takes years to master a foreign language.
She quickly mastered the new software.

senses.def: a person who is very skilled at something
examples: He's a master of suspense in his novels.
The painting is by a Dutch master.

senses.def: a man who has control over servants, animals or a situation
examples: The dog waited patiently for its master to return.

senses.def: (master's) a university degree above a bachelor's
examples: She has a master's in public health.

note: "Master's degree" = yüksek lisans. A "master bedroom" is the largest bedroom in a house.

senses.def: a sports event where two players or teams compete
examples: We watched the tennis match on TV.
The team hasn't lost a match all season.

senses.def: a small stick that produces a flame when you rub it against a rough surface
examples: He lit a match to see in the dark.

senses.def: to be the same as or go well with something, or to find things that go together
examples: Your shoes don't match your belt.
The DNA matched a sample found at the scene.

senses.def: a person or thing that is equal to or goes well with another
examples: The local team was no match for the champions.

note: In American English, "game" is more common than "match" for team sports; "match" is used for tennis, boxing, wrestling.

senses.def: having the same color, pattern or style as something else
examples: The twins wore matching outfits to the party.
She bought a dress and matching shoes.

note: "Matching funds" = money given by an employer or donor equal to what you raise.

senses.def: a friend (informal, British and Australian)
examples: I'm going out with my mates tonight.
Cheers, mate — thanks for the help.

senses.def: used in compounds for someone you share something with
examples: My roommate and I split the rent.
She invited all her classmates to the party.

senses.def: an animal's sexual partner
examples: Male birds sing to attract a mate.

senses.def: to have sex in order to produce young (used about animals)
examples: These whales mate in warm waters.

note: "Mate" for a friend is British/Australian; Americans say "buddy" or "friend". A "running mate" is a vice-presidential candidate.

senses.def: a substance that things can be made from
examples: The house is built from natural materials like wood and stone.
Plastic is a cheap but polluting material.

senses.def: cloth used for making clothes, curtains, etc.
examples: The dress is made of a light cotton material.

senses.def: information or ideas used in books, lessons, comedy shows, etc.
examples: The teacher handed out reading material for the course.
The comedian is testing new material at small clubs.

senses.def: connected with money and possessions rather than the mind or spirit
examples: They have all the material comforts but still feel unhappy.

note: Trap: Turkish "materyalist" also means "maddeci". "Materialistic" in English = caring too much about money and things.

senses.def: connected with or involving mathematics
examples: The model uses complex mathematical equations.
She showed great mathematical ability as a child.

senses.def: very exact or certain
examples: With three games left, the team has only a mathematical chance of winning the league.

senses.def: the science of numbers, quantities and shapes
examples: He has a PhD in applied mathematics.
Mathematics is required for all first-year students.

note: Takes a singular verb: Mathematics is... Americans usually say "math"; the British say "maths".

senses.def: (British) mathematics, especially as a school subject
examples: She got top marks in maths at school in London.
My maths teacher made the subject fun.

note: British only. American English uses "math": I'm good at math.

senses.def: a subject or situation that you must think about or deal with
examples: We have several important matters to discuss today.
This is a private matter between me and my wife.

senses.def: used to ask or say why someone is upset or what the problem is
examples: What's the matter? You look upset.
Is something the matter with your car?

senses.def: to be important or have an effect
examples: It doesn't matter if you're a few minutes late.
Your opinion really matters to me.

senses.def: physical substance that everything in the universe is made of
examples: Plants turn dead organic matter into soil.

note: "No matter how/what/who" = however/whatever/whoever. "It's only a matter of time" = it will certainly happen.

senses.def: behaving in a sensible way, like an adult
examples: She's very mature for a fifteen-year-old.
Let's discuss this in a calm, mature way.

senses.def: fully grown or developed
examples: Mature trees provide shade in summer.
The smartphone market is now very mature.

senses.def: to become fully grown or developed, or to become more sensible
examples: He has matured a lot since he left home.
The wine is left to mature in oak barrels.

note: "Mature content" is a polite label for material with sex or violence, not suitable for children.

senses.tr: en üst düzeye çıkarmak, azami ölçüde artırmak
senses.def: to increase something as much as possible
examples: Companies aim to maximize profits for their shareholders.
Plant the garden in the south to maximize sunlight.

senses.def: to make the best use of something
examples: We need to maximize our limited resources.

note: Opposite: minimize. British spelling: maximise. Also used for enlarging a computer window.

senses.def: as large, fast, etc. as is possible or allowed
examples: The maximum speed on this highway is 70 mph.
The elevator has a maximum load of ten people.

senses.def: the greatest amount, size or number that is possible or allowed
examples: The class has a maximum of twenty students.
Temperatures will reach a maximum of 95 degrees today.

note: Plural: maximums or maxima (formal/scientific). Opposite: minimum. Informal short form: "max".
